market_summary: Monday Oct 12 in Asia: KOSPI -3.65% to 6,384 as Samsung and SK hynix fell more than 3% on Chinese DRAM maker CXMT's 4F2 design progress; Taiwan's Taiex reopened after the holiday flat (-0.02% to 49,302) after a 1.1% intraday dip, with TSMC -0.4%; Shanghai -0.4%, Shenzhen -2.0%; Hang Seng +0.2% and Hang Seng Tech -0.7% in late trade (HK closes 19:00 AEDT); Tokyo shut for Sports Day; ASX 200 +0.8% to 8,783. US futures S&P +0.2-0.3%, Nasdaq +0.2-0.4% ahead of a Columbus Day session with the bond market shut. Brent -1.2% to $103.46 and WTI -1.6% to $90.39 after Trump announced a Russia-Ukraine 'energy ceasefire' that neither side has confirmed, despite a weekend Houthi strike on Riyadh airport that killed 13; gold flat at $4,194, bitcoin about $84,100 (+0.6%). Friday for reference: S&P 500 7,812, Nasdaq 27,366, 10-year 5.24%. Next: US open 00:30 AEDT Tue; Apple home launch 00:00 AEDT Wed; JPM, WFC, Citi and Goldman before the US open Tue (22:00-22:30 AEDT Tue); US CPI 23:30 AEDT Wed; ASML Wed; Anthropic investor session Thu AEDT; TSMC Q3 17:00 AEDT Thu; PPI, retail sales and claims 23:30 AEDT Thu; FOMC blackout from Sat Oct 17; China Q3 GDP 13:00 AEDT Mon Oct 19; Netflix 07:01 AEDT Wed Oct 21.

AMZN.reason: No trading since Friday's close and no weekend company news; Saturday's coverage was opinion pieces only. Alexa tablets go on sale Wed Oct 14 and Q3 results are due around Oct 29 (Fri Oct 30 about 07:00 AEDT). Bank results Tue and US CPI Wed 23:30 AEDT set the macro tone this week. Hold.

AXOS.reason: No weekend company news. Big-bank Q3 results Tue Oct 13 before the US open (about 22:00 AEDT) from JPMorgan, Wells Fargo, Citi and Goldman give the first read on deposit costs and credit ahead of Axos's own fiscal Q1 call on Oct 29 at 5pm ET (Fri Oct 30 08:00 AEDT). Hold.

BABA.reason: Hong Kong shares were up about 1.5% in Monday afternoon trade while Hang Seng Tech fell 0.7%; no company news and nothing new on the Beijing sell-order talk behind Friday's 5.4% jump. China CPI, PPI and trade data Wed Oct 14 at 12:30 AEDT; results Nov 24. Hold until the rally has more than rumour behind it.

ENPH.reason: No weekend company or solar-policy news. Friday's 10-year yield of 5.24% and Mortgage News Daily's 7.48% 30-year rate keep home-solar financing expensive; US CPI Wed 23:30 AEDT is the week's rate catalyst. Q3 call Oct 27 at 4:30pm ET (Wed Oct 28 07:30 AEDT). Watch.

FIGR.reason: No weekend company news and the Q3 results date is still unannounced; the Q2 date was set about four weeks ahead, so a mid-October notice would fit the pattern. Bank results from Tue and US CPI Wed 23:30 AEDT drive the rate-sensitive names this week. Hold.

GOOGL.reason: No weekend company news; Saturday coverage only recapped the Waymo $5 billion loan and the Gemini enterprise agent. Nothing company-specific is scheduled this week and Q3 results come late October. Add stays.

LDI.reason: No weekend company news after Friday's 9% drop to a 52-week low. Mortgage News Daily's 30-year rate ended Friday at 7.48%, its lowest since Sept 25 but still near a two-year high; the US bond market is shut Mon Oct 12 and CPI Wed 23:30 AEDT is the next rate test. Still below the NYSE one-dollar threshold with the cure period to February; trim.

META.reason: No ruling yet from Judge Mathew on the New Mexico privacy penalty: the state asked for $35-40 billion, a legal-news report says Meta's latest brief asks for no more than $1.53 billion, and the judge has said he will rule by late October. No other weekend news. Q3 results late October; hold through the ruling.

MRVL.reason: No weekend company news; the only Saturday item repackaged Bank of America's Oct 8 note (Buy, target raised to $400 from $365) that followed the investor-day targets. Bank results Tue and CPI Wed 23:30 AEDT set the tone, and TSMC's Q3 call Thu 17:00 AEDT is the week's first read on AI demand. Hold.

MU.reason: Korean peers Samsung and SK hynix fell more than 3% Monday after China's CXMT said it plans DDR5 server modules on a denser DRAM design by end-2026, a read-through risk when the US opens tonight. DRAM spot still made new highs Monday (DDR5 16Gb +0.9%). No new Taiwan union news: rally Oct 19, Taichung mediation Oct 22. Hold.

NFLX.reason: Puck reported Friday that Netflix plans a restructuring cutting about 5% of staff (roughly 800 people), possibly announced this week; Netflix declined to comment. Q3 results Tue Oct 20 after the close (Wed Oct 21 07:00 AEDT), with guidance of $12.86 billion revenue (+12%) and a 33.2% operating margin. Cuts help margins but confirm the slower-growth story; hold into the print.

NVDA.reason: The FT reported Saturday that Nvidia is in early talks to buy Reflection AI or deepen its $800 million stake, with an acqui-hire among the options and a deal possible within weeks; Reuters could not verify it. Otherwise no weekend news. TSMC's Q3 call Thu 17:00 AEDT is the first supply-chain read, then GTC Berlin Oct 20-22. Hold.

RKT.reason: No weekend company news. Mortgage News Daily's 30-year rate finished Friday at 7.48%, down 0.02 points on the day and the lowest since Sept 25, while Freddie Mac's weekly 7.40% was still the highest since 2023. The US bond market is shut Mon Oct 12; bank results Tue and CPI Wed 23:30 AEDT set rates for the week. Q3 around Oct 29; watch.

TSM.reason: Taiwan shares fell only 0.4% on Monday's reopen after the holiday, against the ADR's 4% slide on Thu-Fri, so the local market did not join the OpenAI scare. Q3 results Thu Oct 15 at 14:00 Taipei (17:00 AEDT): consensus is about $45.4 billion revenue against the $46.7 billion already reported, gross margin guided 65-67%. Add stays.

STRIPE.reason: No new round, tender or secondary mark over the weekend; the last company tender was February at $159 billion, so the mark multiple stays 2.27. Newsroom items remain the Oct 6 FedEx Dataworks partnership and the Parafin acquisition. Hold.

OPENAI.reason: No weekend movement on the $30 billion round at a $1.4 trillion pre-money valuation; it is still in talks with MGX and BlackRock, so the mark multiple stays 5.43. Friday's AP report that OpenAI fired three safety researchers for a 'breach of trust' (they say it was for prioritising safety) is a governance wobble, not a valuation event. Anthropic's investor session Wed US (Thu AEDT) is the week's private-AI reference point. Hold.

headlines: KOSPI fell 3.65% Monday as China's CXMT showed denser DRAM; Samsung and SK hynix down over 3%, a risk for Micron tonight.
TSMC fell just 0.4% in Taipei after the holiday, far less than the ADR's 4% slide; results Thursday 17:00 AEDT.
FT: Nvidia in early talks to buy Reflection AI or add to its $800M stake; Puck says Netflix plans 5% job cuts.
White House demands transparency from Anthropic over Claude's false police tip, two days before its investor session (Thu AEDT).
AI debt issuance fell to $23B in September from $113B in June; H100 rent dipped 2c to $2.83, DDR5 spot at a new high.
Next: US opens 00:30 AEDT Tue, Apple event 00:00 AEDT Wed, CPI Wed 23:30 AEDT (core seen +0.2%), ASML Wed 16:00 AEDT.
